title: Association between prenatal exposure to alkylphenols and intelligence quotient among preschool children: sex-specific effects.
ehr_evidence: This research was conducted using a subset of mother-child pairs from the Guangxi Zhuang Birth Cohort (GZBC), a prospective population-based study initiated in June 2015, to examine the effects of prenatal environmental exposures on the health outcomes of both mothers and children [23].
summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the association between prenatal maternal serum alkylphenol exposure and childhood intelligence quotient at ages 3-6, including sex-stratified and mixture effect analyses.
key_findings: Each unit increase in log10-transformed maternal NP exposure was associated with a 2.38 (95% CI: -4.59, -0.16) decrease in full-scale IQ.
Maternal 4-T-OP in the second tertile was inversely associated with working memory index (β = -5.24; 95% CI: -9.58, -0.89).
Maternal 4-N-NP in the third tertile was positively associated with fluid reasoning index (β = 4.95; 95% CI: 1.14, 8.77).
Among girls, each unit increase in log10-transformed maternal 4-N-NP exposure was associated with a 13.48 (95% CI: 1.09, 25.87) increase in working memory index.
Among girls, each unit increase in log10-transformed maternal 4-N-OP exposure was associated with a 10.30 (95% CI: 1.18, 19.43) increase in working memory index.
Combined maternal AP mixture exposure above the 50th percentile exhibited a decreasing trend on VCI, VSI, WMI, PSI, and FSIQ in total children and girls.
captured_features: childhood IQ scores (VCI, VSI, WMI, FRI, PSI, FSIQ)
population: 221 mother-child pairs from the Guangxi Zhuang Birth Cohort in China; children aged 3-6 years
limitations: potential unmeasured confounding (e.g., maternal occupation, maternal IQ)
single early-pregnancy serum measurement may cause exposure misclassification
